necessary_context.content: At w the Oracle returns f(w), gradient f(w), and Hessian f(w). Each query w_t is a deterministic function of Oracle responses at preceding queries. Theorem 2 concerns an unconstrained problem on R^d, with dimension allowed to depend on problem parameters.
necessary_context.locator: Section 2.1, PDF p.5; discussion following Theorem 2, PDF p.6
necessary_context.name: Second-order Oracle and deterministic query model

necessary_context.content: mu1, mu2, D, epsilon are arbitrary positive parameters. The hard function is convex and twice differentiable, has globally Lipschitz gradient and Hessian with respective constants mu1 and mu2, and has a global minimizer within Euclidean distance D of the initial query. Accuracy is absolute objective gap at w_T.
